target_customer: Non-programmers, students and hobbyists who want to make 2D games on iPad; revenue mainly from app sales
problem: Making a native mobile game normally requires programming and a desktop toolchain; hyperPad lets people build and publish games from an iPad with visual drag-and-drop logic.
business_model: Paid app (one-time purchase of 14.99 USD) plus free Starter tier
product_category: No-code game creation app for iPad

founders.name: Hamed Saadat
founders.background_notes: YC bio says he works across front end, back end, AI, ML and DevOps.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a visual game engine with physics and a publishing pipeline that runs on iPad is a substantial engineering job for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Engine and editor were copyable by established tools; community content and an app store presence give some lock-in but no sourced strong moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows Apple or others copying it; the app is still sold in 2026.

market_need_then: The iPad was widely used and App Store game publishing was popular, but no source quantifies demand for no-code game tools in 2014.

rebrands.why: Seen only in a search snippet of a MacRumors forum post, not opened (403); date unknown

branding.community_and_virality: Maintains a community hub (hyperPad Hub), a forum and a blog; supports 35 languages per company claims.

brand_strength.rationale: Small niche brand with an active community forum but no independent press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: hyperPad is still sold on the App Store at a one-time price of 14.99 dollars with a free Starter version, and the site shows content through September 2026, so it survived a decade as a small independent tool. No funding beyond YC was found, and growth evidence is limited to the company's own claims, so its outcome is a lasting niche product rather than a venture-scale result.
notes: No funding found: CB Insights lists a 30K USD seed dated May 2013 from DreamIt Ventures under a different record name (untitledd), a single aggregator, unverified and not recorded. YC standard deal not recorded. Name origin: a MacRumors thread snippet says the app was first called tappabl and renamed hyperPad for clarity and to echo HyperCard; the thread returned 403 and was not opened, so not used as fact. No dated 2014 competitor source found; the competitor blog posts on hyperpad.com are vendor marketing from 2025, so the list is empty. Founder education and employers not found. App Store since 2014 per the company site.
